title: Release guardchain: configurable approval pathways for model promotions
creator: Aubrey Chen
description:
We need a flexible, auditable approval mechanism for model promotions that is enforceable by the Console and the control plane. Current ad-hoc signoff processes create friction for multi-team deployments and make post-incident forensics hard. The proposed 'guardchain' is a configurable sequence of gates (policy, human signoff, auto-checks) that must be satisfied before a model can move from staging->canary->prod or be promoted between compatibility tiers. Each gate emits structured audit events and an evidence bundle stored with the release.

Scope: Console UX for building guardchains, backend enforcement during promotion APIs, RBAC integration for gate actors, audit-event schema, evidence-bundles for each promotion, and a minimal developer CLI to attach evidence. Out of scope: full granular policy language (we will support a limited policy DSL for v1).
acceptance_criteria: Admin can create a guardchain with 1..5 gates and name each gate
Each gate can be configured as 'manual signoff', 'policy check', or 'automated smoke test'
Manual signoffs are enforced by RBAC roles (approver groups) and require at least N approvers or quorum
Promotion API rejects promotions that don't satisfy the guardchain and returns actionable failure reasons
Audit log entry (immutable) is created for each gate attempt with a link to the evidence bundle
Evidence bundle stores: artifact id, preflight test summary, latency/cost delta, evaluation snapshot link
Console shows the guardchain state for active promotions and allows owners to attach remediation notes
Auto-rollback policy can be attached to the promotion and fires if production metrics exceed thresholds
decisions: Implement guardchain as a first-class object in the control plane (not just console metadata)
Support three gate types in v1: manual, policy-check (preflight), automated smoke test
Evidence bundles will be stored in internal object store and referenced by immutable audit events
RBAC will use existing group/role model; 'approver' is a new role that can be granted at org or project level
Auto-rollback will be evaluated by the runtime metrics stream and triggered server-side (enforced by routing)
tradeoffs: Limited policy DSL reduces early complexity but will require follow-up work for complex org policies
Storing evidence bundles increases storage cost and retention concerns — retention policy will default to 90 days
Enforcing guardchains server-side adds latencies to promotion API calls; mitigate via async checks with blocking semantics
Tighter RBAC integration reduces product flexibility for early users who prefer informal Slack approvals
